To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a radiation tolerant 1.25Gbit/s serializer was developed, tested and found to be fully operational.

1) a radiation hard serializer ASIC has been designed and implemented in a mainstream technology; 2) the ASIC has been fully characterized in a test setup and error free data transmission at the required speed was achieved; 3) the ASIC has shown to be fully functional in a radiation hard environment.
a 1.25Gbit/s serializer for high speed optical links in LHC detectors has been designed and tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of radiation resistant IC’s for the LHC data and triggers systems that will enable the use of commercial components for high-speed data transmission in the LHC environment.
developing radiation tolerant, high-speed digital optical link ASICs for the transmission of high-speed data in LHC-HEPs radiation hard environments.
the development of radiation hard, high speed, high density, and low power digital ASIC’s for data and trigger links for LHC experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work represents a successful attempt to implement a high-speed serializer ASIC that meets the bandwidth requirements for data transmission in LHC experiments and that is also radiation resistant.
this ASIC is a good example of a successful design of a high speed digital ASIC for the LHC- HEP environment.
a high speed transmitter ASIC (1Gbit/s) has been developed and tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design is radiation hard and the test setup can be used as a test bench for the development of future radiation tolerant optical links.
the prototype is fully functional, and that the radiation hardness of this implementation was successfully demonstrated by means of irradiations with 1MeV electrons.
we have developed an ASIC that is able to serialize 1.2Gb/s data streams and is able to operate in high radiation environments, and we have tested the ASIC in a test setup.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of radiation tolerant ICs is possible using mainstream CMOS technologies.
radiation tolerance can be achieved in high-speed digital ASICs using mainstream CMOS technologies.

the design of radiation tolerant ICs can be based on the use of commercial components, and that radiation tolerant design techniques can be applied to mainstream technologies to achieve the desired level of radiation resistance.
